newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Housing cost rise sees NZ Jun qtr CPI up 0.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Housing cost rise sees NZ Jun qtr CPI up 0.1 pct.

text.p: WELLINGTON, July 15 - The New Zealand consumers price index rose 0.1 percent in the June quarter, Government Statistician Len Cook said on Tuesday.
This follows a fall of 0.3 percent in the March quarter and a rise of 0.7 percent in the December 1996 quarter.

Housing costs contributed the most to the increase rising by 0.8 percent in the June quarter. The cost of renting a house or flat rose, as did the cost of purchasing a section and construction expenses.
Food prices had the next most significant increase, rising by 0.4 percent. Three of the four food subgroups showed an increase this quarter, with grocery food having the most significant price rise.
The rise in the June quarter CPI took the annual rise in the CPI to 1.1 percent, the lowest since the June 1994 quarter.

Statistics NZ said the increase in stationery supplies as they returned to normal after "back to school specials" in conjunction ith the increase in newspaper prices and boarding school accommodation fees led to an overall rise of 0.8 percent in the recreation and education group in June.
Credit services contributed the most significant offsetting movement in the quarter, falling 2.3 percent, mainly due to a fall in mortgage interest rates.

Public transport costs rose and private transport costs fell, resulting in a fall for the transport group of 1.1 percent. The main contribution to the fall came from price falls in both new and used cars.
A rise in electricity prices dominated the 0.4 percent rise in the cost of household operations this quarter.
Overall tobacco and alcohol prices rose 0.5 percent in June, mainly due to an increase in the price of alcoholic drinks.
